clue.text: Pallid article about a classic novel

indicators.note: about means the article's letters go round the novel's title

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
She is the classic adventure novel by H. Rider Haggard

explanation.surface: A pale, faded piece of writing about some old literary classic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a classic novel' is Rider Haggard's She, about the immortal Ayesha; 'about' is the container signal, not 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a face drained of colour, grey and wan.

clue.text: A big, clear form of notation

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: form here is a verb-like signal to shape these letters into something new

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A large, legible way of writing things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges A BIG CLEAR; 'of notation' is the adjectival definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra writes quantities as symbols, so its kind of symbolic writing is described this way.

clue.text: Governor supervising fate of serf :5

indicators.note: in a down clue, supervising puts one word above the other

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of a colonial governor
lot is fate or destiny

explanation.surface: A ruler overseeing what becomes of a peasant.
explanation.walkthrough: His Excellency is the formal style of a colonial governor. Helots were the state serfs of ancient Sparta.
explanation.definitionFit: Helots were the bonded labourers of ancient Sparta, a class of bondmen.

clue.text: Sort of energy not easily perceived when heads change places

indicators.note: the two leading letters swap places, so the first letter moves back one spot

parts.note: unclear means hard to make out

explanation.surface: A kind of power that is hard to see when leaders swap roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when heads change places' swaps the first two letters of UNCLEAR, U and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic power from fission or fusion is the familiar kind meant.

clue.text: Extremely shivery she sent out for combinations

indicators.note: extremely asks for the word's extremes, its first and last letters only
sent out suggests these letters are sent off in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shivering badly dispatches her various mixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes S and Y from 'shivery'; 'out' rearranges SHE SENT into NTHESES.
explanation.definitionFit: Syntheses are things formed by putting elements together, i.e. blends or unions.

clue.text: They loved the introduction of steam wagons

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: wains are farm wagons

explanation.surface: Folk adored the arrival of steam-powered carts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the introduction of' takes S from 'steam'.
explanation.definitionFit: Swains are young country lovers or suitors in pastoral poetry, men who courted.

clue.text: Speculative conversion into loan

indicators.note: a conversion changes something into another form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A risky plan to convert something into a loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' rearranges INTO LOAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Notional means hypothetical or theoretical, existing only in thought.

clue.text: Source of water for hospital to dry out worker

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
a worker is an ant, a common crossword shorthand

explanation.surface: A water supply for a hospital that is drying out a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes YDR from the word dry; 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydrant is a street outlet for drawing water from the mains, used by firefighters.

clue.text: He engages in malicious representation, it has to be said

definitions.text: He engages in malicious representation, it has to be said

parts.words: He engages in malicious representation, it has to be said
parts.note: a false and damaging misrepresentation that is spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: Someone who misrepresents others maliciously, and frankly that must be stated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it has to be said' looks like a throwaway aside, but defamation in speech (rather than print, which is libel) is the precise legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Slander is spoken defamation, so one who utters damaging falsehoods is meant.

clue.text: It was used to write some misty legends

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An ancient tool used for writing down some foggy myths.
explanation.walkthrough: A style, or stylus, was the pointed tool used to scratch letters on wax tablets.
explanation.definitionFit: A style is an old pointed instrument for writing on wax, a stylus.

clue.text: Metal found round old colony

parts.note: gold is a precious metal

indicators.note: round tells us the word for found encircles the abbreviation for old

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: Precious metal discovered near an ancient settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is not 'discovered' but the metalworking verb, CAST, which goes 'round' O. The Gold Coast was the British colony that became Ghana.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gold Coast was a British West African colony before independence as Ghana in 1957.

clue.text: In which we record lines on withdrawal of benefit

indicators.note: in an across clue, lines on something means placed after it
a withdrawal draws the word back, so the word for benefit runs right to left

parts.note: aid is help or benefit
RY is the abbreviation for railway, lines in crosswords

explanation.surface: Keeping a record of the queues when welfare payments are stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: Railway lines are the usual crossword source of RY; 'withdrawal of' turns the benefit word to make DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A diary is a book kept for writing down daily events and appointments.

clue.text: Separating solver and setter? This is in confidence

definitions.meaning: literally lying between the solver (you) and the setter (me)

explanation.surface: Something that comes between the puzzle-solver and its compiler is to be kept secret.
explanation.walkthrough: The solver is 'you' and the setter writing the clue is 'me', so whatever separates them is literally between the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces a remark meant to stay private, a secret shared by two.

clue.text: Wonder at the mud on a notice

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
mire is deep mud

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at mud splattered across a posted sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a placing word here: in an across clue, the mud comes after the notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To wonder at something is to regard it with approval and awe.

clue.text: He takes pains to enjoy himself

definitions.text: He takes pains to enjoy himself

parts.words: He takes pains to enjoy himself
parts.note: takes pains suggests making an effort, but here means literally accepting pain for pleasure

explanation.surface: A man who puts real effort into having a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes pains' is an idiom for trying hard; read literally, it is someone who receives suffering gladly.
explanation.definitionFit: One who derives pleasure from being hurt is so called, after Sacher-Masoch.

clue.text: Deed admitted by secret police chief may make us sick!

indicators.note: admitted by means the word for deed is let inside the chief's name

parts.note: Lavrentiy Beria headed Stalin's secret police, the NKVD
an act is a deed

explanation.surface: An atrocity confessed by the head of the secret police is enough to turn the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: Lavrentiy Beria ran Stalin's NKVD; the exclamation marks the playful definition, germs that cause illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Many microbes are pathogens, the germs behind infections and illness.

clue.text: Cane lad wildly for hiding books of short stories

indicators.note: hiding means the jumbled letters conceal the books inside them
wildly signals that the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Beat a boy furiously for hiding storybooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' makes ANECDAL from the cane and lad; Old Testament books are a crossword staple for OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal means consisting of brief personal tales rather than hard evidence.

clue.text: Tree in east, standing upright in lake

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters inside the name of the lake

parts.note: Garda is the largest lake in Italy

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing upright means the letters read from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree in the east, growing straight up beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing upright' makes ENI; Lake Garda is in northern Italy. 'Tree' is generous for a shrub that can grow tree-sized.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardenia is an evergreen shrub or small tree with fragrant white flowers.

clue.text: One whose records are made available to the public

definitions.text: One whose records are made available to the public

parts.words: One whose records are made available to the public
parts.note: reads like a recording artist or a released file, but points to a guest on the radio show Desert Island Discs, whose chosen discs are broadcast

explanation.surface: A musician or official whose files are released for everyone to see.
explanation.walkthrough: On BBC Radio's long-running Desert Island Discs the guest is the 'castaway', picking eight records to take to an imaginary island; those records are then played to listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: The show casts its guest as a marooned person choosing music, so the record-chooser is the marooned one.

clue.text: Uninhibited behaviour of fellow propping up a bar

indicators.note: in a down clue, propping up means the word sits underneath

parts.note: a ban is a bar, a prohibition
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: Wild conduct from a man leaning on a pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub counter; it is BAN. 'propping up' puts DON beneath A BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandon as a noun means a total lack of restraint, wild freedom.

clue.text: Stout Poles are ultimately few and far between

parts.note: spars are stout poles, such as a ship's masts and booms

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word are

explanation.surface: Sturdy Polish people are, in the end, quite rare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout Poles' looks like people from Poland; it is SPARS. 'ultimately' adds E, the last letter of 'are'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered, scarce and widely spaced.

clue.text: Baseball player in jug

definitions.meaning: the player who throws the ball to the batter

explanation.surface: A ballplayer stuck inside a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: The thrower in baseball and a large pouring jug share this name.

clue.text: The cost of an attack

definitions.meaning: a headlong assault, as by cavalry

explanation.surface: What an assault will cost you.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee is a charge, and so is a cavalry rush at the enemy.

clue.text: Shakespearian horseplay

parts.note: horseplay suggests rowdy fun, but means a history play famous for its king's cry offering his kingdom for a horse

explanation.surface: Rough-and-tumble fooling in a Shakespeare production.
explanation.walkthrough: The play ends with the king crying 'A horse! a horse! my kingdom for a horse!' at Bosworth, so it is a 'horse play'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bard's history drama hinges on a desperate plea for a mount, making it a play about a horse.

clue.text: Summing-up of accountant in theatre

indicators.note: in means the accountant's letters go inside the theatre word

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An accountant's closing summary delivered on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Repertory theatre is shortened to rep; a chartered accountant is a CA.
explanation.definitionFit: A recap, short for recapitulation, is a brief summary of main points.

clue.text: At home, a form of training that's unsuitable

parts.note: in means at home
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: Some home exercise routine that turns out to be inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: PT is physical training, the British name for school gym lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means not fitting or inappropriate.

clue.text: Youngster once told off for pinching money

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing, so the old word for scolded holds the money symbol

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold
L is the abbreviation for a pound, libra

explanation.surface: A youth was scolded long ago for stealing some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks CHID as archaic; 'for pinching' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A child is a young person, a kid.

clue.text: Direction given briefly just before end of journey

definitions.text: Direction given briefly just before end of journey

parts.words: Direction given briefly just before end of journey
parts.note: the abbreviated compass point sits in the word journey immediately before its final letter Y

explanation.surface: A quick instruction issued just as a trip is finishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell out 'journey': its last letter is Y, and just before it come N and E, the short form of this compass bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The compass point midway between north and east is written briefly as NE.

clue.text: River goddess securing shelter for a monarch

indicators.note: securing means the river and goddess together hold the shelter between them

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin
a tent is a portable shelter

explanation.surface: A river deity holding a refuge for a king.
explanation.walkthrough: Ate was the Greek goddess of folly and ruin; the Po is Italy's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: A potentate is a ruler with great power, like a sovereign.

clue.text: Animal seen in lake by 21

parts.note: 21 down is CHARGE, and a charge is a rate

explanation.surface: A creature spotted in a lake beside clue 21.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 21's answer means price, so read it as RATE; 'by' sets L beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel is the honey badger, a fierce African and Asian mammal.
